page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the system exposes 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio aligned with standard compute-focused sizing. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set flags include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI alongside hardware cryptographic support via AES.

Storage and networking configurations emphasize network-attached resources. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external cloud disk volumes for all stateful filesystem operations and persistent data. Hypervisor operations are managed through KVM with fully dedicated CPU core scheduling. Baseline network throughput is rated at 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance.

Synthetic and operational benchmarks position the instance within the mid-range for parallel processing. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng single-core (1310.79) and gzip compression (22.94 GB/sec), sit in the lower quartile, influenced by the moderate 2.5 GHz base clock rate. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads demonstrate solid middle-tier throughput, represented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7270.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15413.0. In-memory and application benchmarks remain consistent, with Redis SET operations sustaining 13.56 million operations per second and static web serving reaching 11.54 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and multi-threaded scaling, the instance offers a resource profile well matched to workloads where high per-core memory capacity is unnecessary. Common deployment fits include distributed CI/CD build environments, Clang-based software compilation, horizontal web serving, reverse proxies, and microservices layers that do not depend on high-speed local disk caches.
